title: Bridge Captain: LibGDX Remake
description: After the original Android release of Bridge Captain, I rebuilt the game in LibGDX as a semi-3D evolution of the C.E.L.L. version. The bridge remained primarily a command-console interface while I added 3D ships, space views, solar-system navigation, procedural planets, terrain generation, scanning, target visualization, and expanded bridge systems. I ultimately moved the project to Unity because my long-term vision was a fully 3D bridge with interactable crew characters rather than a hybrid 2D/3D interface.

sections.title: Semi-3D Remake
paragraphs: The LibGDX generation was designed as a semi-3D port and expansion of the original Android/C.E.L.L. version.
Rather than immediately rebuilding every bridge interaction in full 3D, I kept the proven console-based interface while moving more of the universe and visualization systems into 3D.

sections.title: Hybrid Bridge Architecture
paragraphs: The bridge remained largely a 2D command interface, but individual panels and full-screen modes could render 3D content.
This let me preserve the original bridge workflow while introducing progressively richer 3D systems.

sections.title: 3D Space Views
paragraphs: The remake added a real-time 3D universe around the bridge experience.

sections.title: 3D Navigation
paragraphs: Navigation expanded beyond the original 2D presentation into a 3D solar-system view.
The navigation interface rendered system objects with a perspective camera and allowed the player to inspect the system spatially.

sections.title: Planet Scanning
paragraphs: Planet scanning became a substantial subsystem in the LibGDX remake rather than a simple static report.
A scanned planet could be represented through multiple visual modes including conventional map views, 3D height-map terrain, and generated scan imagery.

sections.title: Procedural Planet & Terrain Generation
paragraphs: I integrated my procedural planet and terrain work directly into Bridge Captain during this generation.
The system used fractal/noise-based generation to create planet maps and height data that could be visualized both in 2D and as 3D terrain.

sections.title: Dynamic 2D-to-3D Scan Pipeline
paragraphs: The scan architecture could render a generated map into a framebuffer and then use that result as a texture on a 3D terrain model.
This connected the bridge's 2D scan presentation directly to the generated 3D planetary representation.

sections.title: Framebuffer Rendering
paragraphs: Framebuffer objects were used to render intermediate visual content that could then be reused elsewhere in the interface or applied to 3D geometry.
This made the bridge panels more than static UI windows; they could act as composited rendering surfaces.

sections.title: Shaders
paragraphs: The LibGDX version used custom shader paths for selected 3D rendering and visual effects.
GLSL became part of the rendering stack alongside LibGDX's model and camera systems.

sections.title: Expanded Bridge Tools
paragraphs: The remake expanded the number and purpose of bridge displays beyond the original release.

sections.title: Target & Diagnostics Views
paragraphs: The architecture included dedicated target-ship and blueprint/diagnostic displays for inspecting ships and other objects.

sections.title: Mining Prototype
paragraphs: Mining had reached at least the interface/prototype stage during this LibGDX generation, with dedicated bridge-panel support.

sections.title: Environment / Walking Prototype
paragraphs: I also experimented with a character-scale environment mode inside the LibGDX branch.
The surviving code includes a 3D environment panel with character rendering and camera movement, showing that I was already exploring gameplay beyond a fixed bridge interface.

sections.title: Remastering While Content Expanded
paragraphs: While additional mission content was being developed, I was rebuilding and extending the technology underneath the game.
This generation therefore acted as both a remaster of the original release and a technology bridge toward the larger version I ultimately wanted to build.

sections.title: Why I Moved to Unity
paragraphs: The LibGDX remake was technically successful as a semi-3D evolution, but it was not my final vision for Bridge Captain.
I wanted the player physically present on a fully 3D bridge with interactable crew characters.
Unity provided a much better foundation for that direction, so I stopped investing in the hybrid LibGDX architecture and moved the project to Unity.

sections.title: Bridge Captain Generation Lineage
paragraphs: This card represents the LibGDX transition generation only.
The original C.E.L.L./Android release and the later fully 3D Unity/VR generations are documented separately.

historicalNotes: The legacy portfolio card was titled 'Bridge Captain Remake (2014)'.
Canonical public title should be 'Bridge Captain: LibGDX Remake'.
This generation was a semi-3D port/evolution of the Android/C.E.L.L. Bridge Captain version, not the final fully 3D design.
The bridge remained primarily a 2D console/interface architecture while ships, space, navigation, planets, terrain, scans, and other content moved into 3D.
Surviving code appears to come from an early 2014 snapshot, with timestamps spanning approximately late November 2013 through February 2014.

The surviving snapshot contains LibGDX PerspectiveCamera, ModelBatch, ModelInstance, lighting, skybox, shader, framebuffer, procedural terrain, planet scanning, navigation, target, diagnostics, mining, and environment-panel work.
The procedural terrain/planet generator previously documented separately is directly integrated into the Bridge Captain LibGDX source and belongs to this project generation.
Surviving terrain classes include FractalGen, Noise, HeightMapTexture, HeightMapModelFactory, Terrain, and TerrainColor.
The code supports 2D planet maps, 3D height-map terrain, generated scan textures, and applying framebuffer-rendered scan imagery to generated terrain.
A mining panel is present, confirming mining had reached at least UI/prototype implementation in this branch.
An EnvironmentPanel provides evidence of early character-scale / walking-environment experimentation.

Do not automatically attribute later trading, faction, broader economy, approximately 10 handcrafted star systems, mature exploration, or later Unity systems to this early LibGDX snapshot unless supported by separate evidence.
Jamie ultimately stopped the LibGDX remake because his intended Bridge Captain design was a fully 3D bridge with interactable characters.
The transition to Unity was an architectural/product-direction decision rather than a failure of the LibGDX implementation.
Later Bridge Captain Unity and VR generations should remain separate portfolio cards.
